subject: Runtime surge lane decision and customer brief
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: staging+alerts@brightcart.com
Date: 2024-11-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [SEV] Runtime surge: p95/p99 jump affecting BrightCart

Team —

We observed a sudden runtime tail at ~09:08 PT across the gen-api fleet serving BrightCart. Key indicators: p95 increased from 220ms -> 1.4s and p99 from 480ms -> 3.6s over a ~8 minute window. Error rates did not materially increase; majority are high-latency responses.

Initial triage notes: 
- Atypical KV cache miss rate spike on the warm path (cache hit rate dropped ~17%)
- Small subset of requests (~0.6%) hit a long-running kernel path with high allocation churn (see attached runtime-metrics-2024-11-20.csv)
- Autoscaler did not react fast enough due to burst smoothing config

Immediate asks: 
1) Can product/CS approve a short customer-facing note we can push to BrightCart OPS (<=30 min)? I drafted a one-paragraph acknowledgement below.
2) Eng: recommend enabling the emergency circuit-breaker to cap concurrency for this tenant and fallback to the quantized variant (if compatible). Karthik, can you confirm rollback/impact?
3) Ops: prepare to roll a targeted canary with the kernel fix if we can validate in staging.

Attachment: runtime-metrics-2024-11-20.csv (summary graphs + sample stack traces)

I will keep the incident bridge open.

— jasmine

--
[attachment: runtime-metrics-2024-11-20.csv]

Subject: Re: [SEV] Runtime surge: p95/p99 jump affecting BrightCart

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Jasmine. Kevin/BC team — apologies for the interruption. Short customer note (please approve edits):

"Kevin / BrightCart Ops — we saw an internal runtime surge affecting response latency for a subset of requests between 09:08–09:16 PT. No customer-visible errors were introduced; we are limiting concurrency and deploying a targeted mitigation to reduce tail latency. We'll follow up with a short technical summary and timeframe for normal operations within 90 minutes."

Product ask for @marissa: if we activate the circuit-breaker and fall back to the quantized model for BrightCart's route, what functional regressions should we call out (e.g., slight tokenization differences, rounding in logits)? We need this in the customer note.

Also: please attach any short blurb I can paste to Kevin. I'm going to hold off sending until we agree on the fallback risks.

— mateo

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2024-11-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [SEV] Runtime surge: p95/p99 jump affecting BrightCart

Short technical recommendation:
- Enable tenant-scoped circuit-breaker immediately: reduce concurrent-inflight to 8 for BrightCart routes (current default 20). This limits long-tail queue buildup.
- Activate model fallback to q4_0 quantized variant (already vetted for BrightCart in prior canary, slight degradation in open-ended generation ~0.5–1% BLEU-equivalent metric, mostly in long-range coherence; negligible on short completion tasks).
- Temporarily relax autoscaler smoothing so new instances can be provisioned faster for the tenant.

Rollback/impact notes:
- Fallback is safe for up to 30% drop in token-level quality for pathological prompts; for typical e-commerce completion tasks BrightCart reports, impact is expected to be unnoticeable.
- We will monitor for correctness regressions via the customer prompt-set (link below) and can revert the fallback within 12 minutes if we observe quality flags.

Confluence quick-check: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Runtime+Surge+Playbook

I can implement the circuit-breaker change now and stage the fallback; need a go-ahead from Product or CS for the customer-facing line about model quality.

— Karthik

[attachment: pb-exec-screenshot.png]

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kevin Liu <kevin@brightcart.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2024-11-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Update: brief on today's latency surge (09:08–09:16 PT)

Kevin — quick update from Redwood:

We detected a short period of elevated response latency for a subset of requests to your gen-api routes (09:08–09:16 PT). Our initial mitigation was to throttle concurrency for your tenant and fall back to a quantized model variant for the affected routes. That reduced observed tail latency — p95 returned to ~230ms and p99 to ~480ms within 6 minutes.

What this means for BrightCart:
- Functionally your requests completed as before; we did not observe increased error rates.
- The quantized fallback can introduce minor differences on very long, open-ended prompts (our internal tests show ~0.5–1% delta on a long-form coherence metric). For standard checkout and itemization completions you should not see material changes.
- We will keep monitoring; expect a short post-incident summary with metrics and next steps by EOD.

If you'd like a 15-minute call to run through the timeline and any questions, I'm available this afternoon.

Thanks for bearing with us — we'll follow up with the technical write-up and any permanent fixes.

— Mateo Alvarez
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
